note: RISK-ONLY SCOPE. Sanctions: no OFAC SDN / UN / EU / UK / BIS Entity List designation for JCB India Limited or its UK parent J.C. Bamford Excavators was found in the sources reachable during this run — but this is NOT a verified negative: the DuckDuckGo search backend was down (connection refused) and Google returned HTTP 429, so no sanctions-list screening page could actually be opened. sanctions_hit is therefore null = not verified, not 'clean'. Recommend re-screening against OFAC SDN, EU consolidated, UK OFSI and BIS lists before any decision. Court cases: JCB India is a very frequent litigant, but the pattern is overwhelmingly tax/excise writ petitions and appeals where the company is the PETITIONER (i.e. it is suing the tax authorities), plus one consumer revision and one commercial suit against Action Construction Equipment. The one genuinely adverse-looking matter is the Competition Commission of India case that reached the Supreme Court on 15.01.2019 (JCB India as respondent) — antitrust/dealer-territory issue; per project rules this is noted neutrally and is not a rejection ground. Source for all court entries: Indian Kanoon search results page (https://indiankanoon.org/search/?formInput=JCB%20India%20Limited, 3115 hits, top 10 reviewed). Rating: no CRISIL/ICRA/CARE/India Ratings action for JCB India Limited could be retrieved — search engines returned only generic JCB marketing pages; rating = null, not public in what was reachable. News risk: only parent-group controversies (EU antitrust, Israeli settlements, tax havens, Covid loan) from the Wikipedia article on J.C. Bamford Excavators; these attach to the UK parent, not to the Indian entity, and are neutral notes. RF/CIS supply: a targeted Indian Kanoon query for 'JCB India Russia' returned only 3 unrelated documents (a VAT Act, an NGT case, a Madras HC criminal revision) — no evidence of supplies to Russia or CIS found, but absence of litigation is not absence of trade; rf_supply = null (not verified). No negative news, regulator action or criminal matter involving the Indian entity itself was found. Per Rule 2, none of the above is a rejection ground. Caveats: legal identity, HS code and shipment volumes deliberately not researched per role scope; the input name string mixes a works contractor ('Chechi Construction Company', 'Dhananjaya') with JCB India Ltd — these appear to be separate parties in a tender/works-contract record and should be split before further checks.
